title: Prithu milks the earth: peace for sky and trees
word: the Gayatri and the peace chants
hookLine: a king hunts the earth with a bow, and learns to ask her instead
carry: earth, waters and trees are holy; peace starts there
tomorrow: Priya's assembly team is fighting. is there a chant for that?
last: KEPT BY SOUND, OPENED BY MEANING.

lines: THE EARTH HOLDS BACK THE GRAIN.
A KING HUNTS HER WITH A BOW.
SHE GIVES, AND IS CALLED PRITHIVI.
cards: In the Vishnu Purana, the people of a new king, Prithu, are starving: the earth has held back every plant and grain. Prithu takes up his bow and goes after her.
The earth turns into a cow and runs through every world, and everywhere, there he is. At last she turns and pleads: if you kill me, how will your people live?
So he lowers the bow, and the earth, like a cow for her calf, gives back every plant and grain. She becomes like a daughter to him, the story says, and that's why she's called Prithivi.
Now, a long way from that famine: Priya's rehearsal went badly, and Sam marched her out to the parking lot to look at a tree. It helped, which annoyed her.

teach.h: SKY, AIR, EARTH, WATERS, PLANTS, TREES.
teach.b: A peace chant from the Yajurveda moves in the same order as that walk outside. Dyauh shantih: the sky, peace. Antariksham shantih: the air between sky and earth, peace.
Prithivi shantih: the earth, peace, her name from that story. Apah shantih: the waters, peace. Oshadhayah shantih: the plants, the very ones the earth gave back, peace.
Vanaspatayah shantih: the trees, peace. Then it widens, to the gods, to everything, and only at the very end does it turn: may that peace come to me. Here's the teaching under it.
In Hinduism, the sky, the earth and the waters aren't scenery. They're holy.
The earth is Bhudevi, a goddess and a mother; even a king with a bow had to ask her, not break her.
Rivers are goddesses: the Ganga is Ganga Ma, Mother Ganga. Plants are honored: many homes keep a tulsi plant, holy basil, and water it each morning.
Some families say a short verse before their feet touch the floor, asking Mother Earth to forgive them for stepping on her.
So the chant can't start with me; it walks inward and arrives at one human being last of all. Here's where it meets now. Priya's peace didn't come from fixing the rehearsal.

teach.h: PEACE STARTS WITH THE HOLY WORLD.
teach.b: The chant would say that's the right order: peace for the holy world first, then for me, because I live inside it, not above it.

how: This peace chant from the Yajurveda is recited at the close of some rituals and gatherings, ending with shanti said three times. Many Hindu homes tend a tulsi plant, and some families greet the earth with a verse before stepping out of bed.

p: a king who chased the earth, then asked

s: in the Vishnu Purana, King Prithu destroys the earth to feed his people
she pleads, he lowers his bow, and she gives back every plant and grain.
this peace chant asks peace only for people
it starts with the sky and moves through air, earth, waters, plants and trees.
the chant ends by asking that peace come to me
after the whole holy world, it arrives at one person, last.

games.q: your kid asks why a peace prayer bothers with the sky and the trees instead of just people. which answer matches the chant?
o: because the earth, the waters and the trees are holy, so peace starts with them and comes to people last.
it's a weather prayer, for rain at the right time.
people aren't in it at all; it's only for nature.
games.why: the earth is Bhudevi, a goddess and a mother who gives. the chant walks inward, sky to trees, and only at the end says: may that peace come to me.

practice: If you can, walk slowly to a window or a door. On the way, name each thing as the chant does: sky, air, earth, water, a plant, a tree, even if the water is a glass on the table.
At the end, if it's part of your practice, touch the floor with your fingertips, the way many Hindus greet the earth each morning. Then stand still and breathe there until the time runs out.

wordCard.voice: The Gayatri and the peace chants. Today's piece: dyauh shantih, sky, peace, a chant that honors the holy world before it reaches me.
